adjudicator: primary assistant, source-based adjudication requested by Pranjal
scope: Exactly the 48 historical-versus-fresh disagreements among the 50 re-audited environments. Other configurations and Forced-Perspective Moving Day are outside this adjudication.
raw_artifacts_policy: Original reviewer reports, receipts, comparison data, and historical labels are unchanged. This file is the final-label overlay for these 48 identities.

clockwork_l2.label: no
clockwork_l2.decisive_rule: Clause (iii): an irreversible missed acceptance window is excluded by C_Delta.
clockwork_l2.reason: I mark both L2 interfaces No. A release inside its accepted phase band remains successful throughout that band. Passing beyond a required shaft's last usable band makes this attempt unsalvageable; it is not a recoverable loss of an action opportunity. The two-shaft profile cannot complete another revolution and still finish both shafts within 125 ticks. In normalized drive units the total work rate is 3 per tick; the earliest authored final release is tick 70, an extra turn costs at least 240 units, and both tolerance bands save at most 40. Recovery would require at least 136.67 ticks. Braking, re-engagement, and the changed input surface do not reverse shaft motion or add this missing work budget.

source_evidence.claim: Two-shaft generation, authored release ranges, ratios, load redistribution and finite tick budget.
Successful final state requires every clutch released and every phase inside tolerance.
Both input surfaces share the same forward-only phase dynamics.

palimpsest_l2_full.label: no
palimpsest_l2_full.decisive_rule: The moving echo does not require a motion-dependent capture policy.
palimpsest_l2_full.reason: I reject the reviewer's Yes. L2 has exactly one echo with base [128,122]. Across every allowed phase, period, and radius, its distance from that fixed point is at most sqrt(17^2+13^2)=21.40 pixels, well inside the 40-pixel lock radius. After the static scan/polarization preparation, a hold and the required timed track samples at that point remain valid throughout the echo's motion. A deliberately off-center pointer slipping is not evidence that the optimal capture policy needs prediction.

source_evidence.claim: Single fixed base and bounded sinusoidal displacement.
Hold success is gated by distance, track count, and duration.
Replay applies the same positional and duration requirements.

palimpsest_l3_l5_simplified.label: yes
palimpsest_l3_l5_simplified.decisive_rule: Clauses (i), (ii), and (iii) hold for acquisition; the pre-run override does not apply.
palimpsest_l3_l5_simplified.reason: I reject the reviewer's No. MOVE GLASS leaves a stationary chosen coordinate; CAPTURE ECHO tests its distance from the currently moving echo before automatic tracking starts. A formerly valid coordinate can cease to capture while the echo remains visible and a corrected coordinate still succeeds. The generated support includes paths wider than twice the lock radius, so the L2 fixed-center argument does not extend across these configurations. Recent motion supports a 200-ms acquisition prediction within the six-frame, 600-ms window. Even at the fastest allowed motion, lock_radius + maximum_speed*200 is below lens_radius: an echo that can be captured after that delay is already observable through the correctly tuned lens. The autonomous phase starts at rendering, not at CAPTURE ECHO. Automatic tracking completes one accepted hold, not the five-echo task; the next echo still requires new polarization/coordinate/capture actions during ongoing motion. Calling each accepted hold a pre-run solution incorrectly discards the acquisition being classified.

source_evidence.claim: Distance is tested before automation; motion starts at render and each accepted hold advances only one echo.
Five echoes, changing polarizations, generated motion radii and periods.
Coordinate-capture start and automatic tracking use the same replayed moving positions.

dead_mans_switch_l1_full.label: no
dead_mans_switch_l1_full.decisive_rule: A stationary pointer remains within the pressure acceptance region for every allowed motion.
dead_mans_switch_l1_full.reason: I reject the reviewer's Yes. Keeping the held pointer at normalized track center [0.5,0.5] is safe for every L1 phase: (175/270)^2+(115/310)^2≈0.5577<1. The runtime automatically records pressure samples while the stored pointer remains inside; it does not require corrective pointer movement. The route can therefore be completed with a stationary hold. An edge-positioned pointer that later slips does not establish a need to predict the plate.

source_evidence.claim: Elliptical pressure acceptance predicate.
Sampling advances automatically; the route and pressure controls are separate.
Motion amplitudes are bounded by the substantially larger hit ellipse.

membrane_l1_l2.label: no
membrane_l1_l2.decisive_rule: At least two of the three equally likely courses have successful pre-run solutions.
membrane_l1_l2.reason: I retain No in both interfaces. L1 and L2 contain one marble and uniformly choose one of three fixed courses. Set the four posts to [0.08,0.68,0.32,0.92] for the left course or [0.68,0.08,0.92,0.32] for the right course, then release. With no further post changes, the authored damped trajectory clears the required ordered rings and enters its well below the capture-speed limit. Both courses pass the actual grader at both levels and with each mode's required input source. The resulting lower bound is 2/3, above the 50% override; no claim about the third course is needed.

source_evidence.claim: Uniform shuffled choice of three fixed courses and one round at L1/L2.
Damped-motion replay accepts the unchanged pre-set tensions through capture.
Both interfaces allow tension preparation before release.

occlusion_l1_l2.label: no
occlusion_l1_l2.decisive_rule: Static port preparation and untimed final identity selection do not meet the shared-phenomenon requirement.
occlusion_l1_l2.reason: I retain No. L1 has no hidden transfer. L2 has one real inspection port and no decoy ports: the Full lens can be left at that static port before BEGIN, and the Simplified relay can be selected during the fixed preview. Inspection samples then accumulate automatically during the shuffle. The agent need not predict motion to choose an expiring inspection action. The final shell choice is made after motion stops; any identity information that must be remembered from an earlier shuttle display is a memory requirement, not sufficient recent-window predictive control.

source_evidence.claim: L1/L2 transfer and port generation.
Stored lens or relay selection supplies inspection samples automatically; final selection follows the shuffle.
Inspection evidence and stopped-carrier selection are replayed separately.

grill_all.label: no
grill_all.decisive_rule: Clause (iii) fails on the salvageable set; L1 additionally has a common fixed serving schedule.
grill_all.reason: I retain No at all five levels and in both modes under the settled definition. Cooking is monotone raw-to-ready-to-spoiled, each food has exactly one start and one serve, and every food must pass. Serving within its accepted interval preserves the same outcome; once that food's interval expires, there is no reset, replacement, or recooking transition that can rescue the same attempt. Those missed-window histories are excluded from C_Delta rather than providing a recoverable strict loss. Starting remaining foods within the rush window adds an own-action-clock deadline, not a separate visible predictive process. L1 also permits all three target assignments to be served at a common age of 6000 ms. The No label does not mean that cooking or missed timing has no effect; it follows from the narrower conjunction being used.

source_evidence.claim: Monotone cooking and one-way prep-to-grill-to-tray transitions.
One start and one serve per food; all foods must be accepted; rush rule uses start timestamps.
Randomized target assignment and finite tolerance intervals.
The authoritative ledger rejects repeated starts or serves.

handshake_l1.label: no
handshake_l1.decisive_rule: A constant prepared direction and contact complete the single relay automatically.
handshake_l1.reason: I retain No for both L1 interfaces. After observing the pulse direction, set matching receiver drive and keep contact engaged. Relative motion is 7 degrees per tick until the receiver enters the 30-degree capture band. The runtime then snaps the receiver to the pulse every locked tick; the same held inputs accumulate all eight required charge ticks and automatically relay. There is only one stage. Grader replay succeeds for all 360 initial relative offsets and both pulse directions without any later direction/contact correction, well inside the 420-tick budget.

source_evidence.claim: Accepted ticks snap receiver to pulse and accumulate charge.
Held inputs persist and relay happens automatically.
One stage, +/-1 pulse speed, 8-degree drive, 30-degree tolerance and eight hold ticks.

slot_l1_l4.label: no
slot_l1_l4.decisive_rule: Clause (ii): the 800-ms window does not determine the upcoming symbol/phase in every active-reel history.
slot_l1_l4.reason: I retain No for L1-L4 in both modes. At these levels the symbol is stationary within each token interval and capture becomes valid immediately at a target-token boundary. The target/order/interval can have been learned earlier yet be absent from all six recent frames. Identical recent decoy displays and identical own-action histories can precede different next symbols or different boundary times, so an arbitrary positive delay can straddle an unseen target opening. Full mode additionally needs its character; Simplified mode still must distinguish capture from wait. Restricting the grouped mode to frames currently displaying the target would discard the decoy histories of the same active capture control. There is no early visible capture-band approach at these levels.

source_evidence.claim: Randomized target insertion, symbol order, phase and interval.
L1-L4 use capture_window_ratio=1 and zero within-token displacement.
Acceptance depends on the delivered action's current token; a wrong capture consumes a strike.

slot_l5.label: yes
slot_l5.decisive_rule: The visible pre-capture travel makes a sufficiently short delayed action predictable.
slot_l5.reason: I reject the reviewer's No for both L5 interfaces. L5 alone uses capture_window_ratio=0.68 and displays the symbol moving through a marked capture band. A token is visible for 0.16*interval_ms before capture opens: at least 43.2 ms for every generated interval. Choose Delta=30 ms, not the reviewer's 240 ms. Every symbol that can be accepted at delivery is therefore already displayed at observation time; an unseen next token cannot become capturable within that delay. The six-frame 800-ms window reveals the current position and velocity; the four allowed speeds have distinct 160-ms displacements modulo the visible wrap. Capture the observed alphanumeric symbol only if its predicted position is inside the band, otherwise wait. Crossing the band's trailing edge makes that same key/click lose value within the delay while later cycles remain available. The reviewer incorrectly extended the unseen-token counterexample to every positive delay despite this visible lead-in. No pre-run solution can replace the six separate accepted captures.

source_evidence.claim: 0.68 capture ratio and 270/300/330/360-ms token intervals.
92-pixel visible within-token travel and explicit central capture band.
The symbol and band are rendered, including travel before entry and after exit.
The authoritative acceptance predicate uses the same central-band timing.

first_change_full.label: no
first_change_full.decisive_rule: The transient evidence remains recoverable and actionable in the frozen review timeline.
first_change_full.reason: I retain No for Full at all five levels. After the live animation, the review slider can revisit both the pre-change and changed timestamps while the lens remains movable. The grader explicitly accepts observe events with mode='review' for every required pre-hit and change-hit. Holding the slider at a chosen time supplies repeated observations without tracking the live event. Returning to the settled board and selecting the carrier is then untimed. A missed live view therefore does not destroy the required evidence; it is permanently archived rather than an expiring action opportunity.

source_evidence.symbol: review slider / lens observation / return handlers
source_evidence.claim: The recorded field can be scrubbed and observed after the live phase.
Both live and review observations satisfy the same evidence quotas.

wrong_number_l1_l3.label: no
wrong_number_l1_l3.decisive_rule: Pre-run tuning can satisfy the entire qualification trial without live correction.
wrong_number_l1_l3.reason: I retain No in both interfaces. After identifying the authentic carrier and cancelling its static skew, L1 and L2 can hold the initial phase setting throughout the trial: their maximum drift is smaller than phase tolerance. At L3 a one-step phase bias toward the coming drift keeps error at most 1.34 steps during the 3.6-second trial, below the 1.45-step tolerance (still below tolerance through the next scheduled sample). Drift direction can be observed in a preparation trial; even a fixed bias direction covers half the symmetric generated drift choices. No phase/shape adjustment is required during the successful outcome phase.

source_evidence.claim: Qualification depends on normalized phase, skew, and distortion residuals.
Trials start at elapsed zero and can be prepared and retried with fixed settings.
Drift, tolerance, sample interval and trial-duration bounds.
